rows: Denser oceanic plate subducts under lighter oceanic plate
Dense oceanic plate subducts under lighter continental plate

items: Subduction zones along convergent boundaries are the primary driver of volcanic arcs and deep ocean trenches in the Ring of Fire.
The Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth, formed due to the subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Philippine Sea Plate.
Distinguish between Island Arcs (Oceanic-Oceanic subduction) and Continental Volcanic Arcs (Oceanic-Continental subduction) for prelims questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Pacific Ring of Fire is a 40,000 km horseshoe-shaped region along the Pacific Ocean basin prone to frequent earthquakes and volcanic activity.
It is primarily defined by convergent plate boundaries where tectonic subduction occurs.
Over 75% of the world's active volcanoes and 90% of all earthquakes occur within this seismic belt.
Famous geological features in this zone include the Mariana Trench, the Andes Mountain Range, and the Japanese Archipelago.
